claims.claim_vi: The source names eight programming paradigms (imperative, declarative, object-oriented, aspect-oriented, functional, reactive, generic, concurrent) with one or two sentences and example languages each; the lesson keeps the eight names and groups them in three sets of its own, without reusing the definitions or the language lists.

claims.claim_vi: Python functional HOWTO: procedural programs are lists of instructions telling the computer what to do with its input (C, Pascal, Unix shells); declarative languages let you write a specification of the problem and the implementation decides how to compute it, SQL being the example; object-oriented programs manipulate objects with internal state and methods (Smalltalk, Java; C++ and Python support but don't force it); functional programming decomposes a problem into functions that ideally only take inputs and produce outputs, discourages side effects, and purely functional functions have none (ML family, Haskell); Lisp, C++ and Python are multi-paradigm.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: OOP is an approach in which data is encapsulated within objects and the object itself is operated on rather than its component parts.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Spring documentation: AOP complements OOP; the unit of modularity in OOP is the class and in AOP the aspect; aspects modularize concerns such as transaction management that cut across multiple types and objects.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).
